quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
rationale: Substantively the warranty package sits at our preferred position, so the only open item is a drafting/verification point, which is why this is flagged for review rather than as a deviation. Scope and remedy: § 19.1 warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications; § 19.3 covers Applicable Law compliance and no intentionally introduced malicious code (plus no mid-term functionality diminution and no copyleft contamination of Customer source code); § 19.4 gives prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge escalating to termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; § 19.5 is a mutual implied-warranty-only disclaimer that expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or stated remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty and no carve-out is needed. Duration: § 19.2 gives Deliverables a ninety-day conformance warranty measured from the later of delivery or acceptance (meeting the preferred 90-day benchmark), and Hosted Services conformance for the whole subscription term, which under § 8.2 runs the Order Form initial term plus successive twelve-month renewals. The period is spelled only in words ("ninety days"), with no numeral anywhere in the Agreement, which makes the duration hard to verify mechanically and has twice been misread as a missing or short period. We therefore propose a single clarifying edit inserting the numeral — "ninety (90) days" — with no change to the agreed period, scope or remedies. Only immaterial gaps remain (refund of "Fees paid" rather than "paid or payable"), which the playbook directs be noted rather than flagged.
